planRow: OPS-19b item 6 (setback-value resolution gap for Hays/McLennan/Williamson in-city parcels) follow-up
topic: Round Rock's setback citations are a distinct, separately-fixable problem from Waco/Kyle's -- a real code-section atom corpus exists but doesn't carry the cited numbers, not corpus absence
requestedBy: doc-repo-2c (asked this get its own note rather than be folded into 'one of the relabeled three')
checkpoint: NOTE -- not a close, a flagged distinction worth keeping visible
background: hauska-engine#389 (Waco/Round Rock/Kyle setback tables) shipped provenance claiming verification_state 'human-verified'/'asserted' against a fabricated atom_did convention ID, never checked against the setback extraction acceptance gate (gate.ts lives in legacy-design-tools, no wiring from hauska-engine). Belton's research agent independently ran the real gate and got 254 G2 blocks, which surfaced the gap for the whole batch. Fixed for hauska-engine's three files in PR #393, using the new VerificationState 'primary-source-verified' added in legacy-design-tools#628.

theDistinction.wacoAndKyle: waco_tx and kyle_tx have ZERO code-section atoms in the live atoms store (entity_type='code-section') -- confirmed by direct query, not assumed from the 'ingestion out of scope this sprint' note in legacy-design-tools' setbacks/README.md (that note is real but doesn't mean literally zero everywhere, which is exactly the mistake this note is correcting for anyone who reads it next). No real atom exists anywhere for either jurisdiction to cite. atom_did removed entirely from their provenance.
theDistinction.roundRock: round_rock_tx has 361 real, legitimately-ingested code-section atoms. The two sections round-rock-tx.json actually cites (1-50, 2-26) are genuinely among them -- confirmed by direct query and reading their real bodyText. But: section 1-50's ingested atom is only the section's purpose-statement preamble ('The purpose of this section is to define words, terms and phrases...') plus amendment history -- it does not contain the 'Front Lot Line' definition text actually quoted. Section 2-26's ingested atom is prose about setback ENCROACHMENT EXCEPTIONS (eaves, fireplaces, accessory buildings) -- the section's own 'Residential Lot and Building Dimensional Standards' CHART, which is what actually holds the front/rear/side-ft numbers cited, is referenced in the bodyText only as a placeholder ('(a) Residential zoning districts lot and building dimensional standards chart:') with no cell values captured as text. This is a table/chart text-extraction gap in the ingestion pipeline, not a missing-source problem -- the chart exists in the real ordinance and was ingested as an atom, its cell values just didn't survive into bodyText.

whyThisMatters: These are different bugs with different fixes. Waco/Kyle need real code-section ingestion to exist at all for those jurisdictions (an out-of-scope-this-sprint gap per Spec 51 OQ-1) before any citation there could ever be atom-verified. Round Rock's fix is narrower and already in scope: re-extract sections 1-50 and 2-26 (or just 2-26, since that's where all four numeric fields' real values live) with the actual chart/table content captured as text, and its existing citations could very plausibly become genuinely G5-round-trippable without any new research -- the numbers already cited are correct, they just need a better-extracted atom to check against. Conflating this with Waco/Kyle's total-absence case would incorrectly imply Round Rock also needs to wait on the code-ontology-ingestion program shipping broadly, when it specifically only needs one table's re-extraction.
whatWasDoneTonight: hauska-engine#393 corrected Round Rock's atom_did from a fabricated convention ID to the real entityId for each section (for traceability) and relabeled verification_state to 'primary-source-verified' alongside Waco/Kyle, since today's ingested bodyText genuinely can't support a real round-trip for either one. This is the honest state given what exists right now -- it is not a claim that Round Rock is stuck in the same bucket as Waco/Kyle going forward.
openFollowUp: Not picked up by anyone yet as of this note: re-extracting round_rock_tx section 2-26 (and possibly 1-50) with the dimensional-standards chart's actual cell values captured as text, which would let Round Rock's existing, already-correct citations be promoted to a real G2+G5 pass without new field research. Whoever owns code-section ingestion quality is the natural owner; flagging here so it isn't lost inside the relabel PR's diff.
